series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: "Liberia's INDC includes one component on mitigation and one on adaptation. The extent of implementation of the intended contributions on mitigation and adaptation are conditioned upon the provision of adequate means of implementation by the international community (financial resources, capacity building and the transfer of technologies)." Liberia's mitigation contribution is to reduce total GHG emissions by 15% below a Business-As-Usual trajectory by 2030, through the implementation of four mitigation actions. Liberia's adaptation contribution is to implement actions in seven key sectors - agriculture, energy, health, forestry, coastal zone, fishery, and transport/infrastructure.
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: 15% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to the BAU trajectory
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

evidence.sentence: NDC 2.0, launched in 2021, set a total target to reduce GHG emissions by 64% below business-as-usual (BAU) levels by 2030, comprised of a 10% unconditional reduction to be achieved with the country's own resources and a 54% conditional reduction contingent on receiving international support.

Liberia's NDC 2.0 (launched in 2021) outlined the country's commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 10% unconditionally and up to 54% conditionally by 2030, relative to a business-as-usual scenario.
The country committed to a 64% emissions reduction by 2030 compared to a business-as-usual (BAU) scenario, which projected emissions of 12,429 GgCO2e by 2030.

evidence.sentence: In its revised NDC, Liberia commits to reducing its economy-wide greenhouse gas emissions by 64% below the projected business-as-usual level by 2030, through a combination of the following: unconditional GHG reductions of 10% below BAU, resulting in an absolute emissions level of 11,187Gg CO2e in 2030; with an additional 54% reduction conditional upon international support, which would result in an absolute emissions level of 4,537Gg CO2e in 2030.
The 2015 NDC aimed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 15% below business-as-usual levels by 2030 with a long-term goal of carbon neutrality by 2050, conditional upon international support.

3.0 CONTRIBUTIONS 3.1 Mitigation Liberia commits to reducing its economy-wide greenhouse gas emissions by 64% below the projected business-as-usual level by 2030, through a combination of the following: unconditional GHG reductions of 10% below BAU, resulting in an absolute emissions level of 11,187Gg CO2e in 2030; with an additional 54% reduction conditional upon international support, which would result in an absolute emissions level of 4,536.64 Gg CO2e in 2030.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is NDC 3.0, filed 2025-09-24. 48 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (2). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-35 24.5 MtCO₂e, DS-02 6.5 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 1 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 35.7 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 15% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to the BAU trajectory It was classed conditional. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.03°C under SSP1-2.6 to +3.6°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
